docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
Hi, I am Sheethal U, a Quality Assurance and Technical Writing professional specializing in API validation, automated documentation pipelines, and developer experience (DX).

This repository showcases a collection of well-structured, tested and developer-friendly API documentations written in Markdown.

docs.text:

By authoring technical functional documents, managing release communications, and collaborating closely with engineering teams. docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Loan Search API is organized around REST. It provides internal backend services for dashboard applications to query loan records, populate search filters, and authenticate administrative sessions.

The API accepts JSON-encoded request bodies, returns standard JSON responses, and uses predictable HTTP response codes, verbs, and JWT authentication.

Base URL: https://a8fcbf71-9a93-43f6-ab3c-b95b953b1c57.mock.pstmn.io/

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
To ensure consistent data querying across dashboard applications, search parameters adhere to strict validation logic. Client applications can query application records using three primary text identifiers: Acknowledgement Number, Reference Number, and Application ID. These fields accept 1–15 case-insensitive alphanumeric characters.

Filtering by application status is constrained to three supported statuses: Approved, Pending, and Rejected. For Year filters, the system defaults to 2026, but also allows querying records from previous two consecutive years 2024 and 2025. Result sets can be sorted in ascending or descending order by Submission Date, Amount, or Customer Name.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Errors are returned using standard HTTP error code syntax. Depending on the status code, the response body may be in JSON or plaintext.

Search API uses conventional HTTP response codes to indicate the success or failure of an API request along with clear error messages. In general: Codes in the 2xx range indicate success. Codes in the 4xx range indicate an error that failed given the information provided (e.g., a required parameter was omitted).

HTTP Status Code Summary

docs.title: API reference (detailed)
docs.text: This endpoint verifies a user’s identity before they can access the loan application portal and protected services. Staff sign in with a username and password to search, review, and manage loan records securely. Once the credentials are validated, the API returns a JWT that authorizes subsequent requests. This approach keeps access controlled, supports role-based permissions, and maintains a secure session for daily loan operations.

docs.title: Login (auth)
docs.text:
• URL: /auth/login
  • Method: POST
  • Authentication: Not required for this endpoint
  • Content-Type: application/json
  • Description: Validates a user’s credentials and returns an access token for subsequent authenticated requests. Positive case returns 200 OK with token details; negative cases include invalid credentials, missing fields, and server-side authentication failures.

docs.title: AUTHENTICATION API – SCHEMAS
docs.text:
Model: AuthRequest

Field Type Required Description username string Yes Login username of the user. password string Yes Account password.

AuthRequest

username: `string (required)`
password: `string (required)`
Field Type Required Description status string Yes Response status returned by the authentication service. token string (JWT) Yes Access token used for authentication. expiresIn number Yes Expiration time in seconds. issuedAt string (ISO 8601) Yes Timestamp when the token was issued. roles array[string] Yes The user’s roles and permissions.

AuthResponse

status: `string`
token: `string (JWT)`
expiresIn: `number`
issuedAt: `string (ISO 8601 datetime)`
roles: `array[string]`

docs.title: Example request
docs.text:
{
  "username": "loan.officer",
  "password": "Test@123"
}

docs.title: Success response: 200 OK
docs.text:
{
  "status": "success",
  "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1Ni...",
  "expiresIn": 3600,
  "issuedAt": "2025-01-20T10:20:30Z",
  "roles": [
    "LoanOfficer",
    "ReadOnlyUser"
  ]
}

docs.title: Error responses
docs.text:
• 400 Bad Request — Missing or malformed request fields such as username or password.
  • 401 Unauthorized — Invalid username or password.
  • 500 Internal Server Error — Authentication service failure or unexpected backend error.

Example: 400 Bad Request

{
  "status": "error",
  "errorCode": "ERR_INVALID_INPUT",
  "message": "username and password are required"
}

Example: 401 Unauthorized

{
  "status": "error",
  "errorCode": "ERR_INVALID_CRED",
  "message": "Invalid username or password."
}

Example: 500 Internal Server Error

{
  "status": "error",
  "errorCode": "ERR_500",
  "message": "Authentication service unavailable."
}

docs.title: Endpoint reference (detailed)
docs.text: Before a user can search or filter loan applications in the dashboard, the frontend application calls this endpoint to populate the filter menus. It returns the pre-defined reference options for loan status flags and submission years.

docs.title: Dropdown options
docs.text:
• URL: /dropdown/filters
  • Method: GET
  • Authentication: Bearer <token> (JWT) required in Authorization header
  • Content-Type: application/json
  • Description: This API will returns the loan application status and application year dropdown options that is available in the search filter. Positive case returns 200 OK.

docs.title: Endpoint reference (detailed)
docs.text: This endpoint helps loan staff find application records using relevant filters and sorting options. It supports reviewing applications by acknowledgment number, application ID, status, reference number, and application year. Staff can sort the results by submission date, amount, or customer name in ascending or descending order. These search and sorting capabilities help staff compare records and complete loan review workflows efficiently.

docs.title: Search loan applications
docs.text:
• URL: /search-loans
  • Method: POST
  • Authentication: Bearer <token> (JWT) required in the Authorization header
  • Content-Type: application/json
  • Description: Searches loan applications using request-body filters and optional query parameters. Returns 200 OK with matching records, 400 Bad Request for invalid input, or 404 Not Found when no records match.

docs.title: SEARCH API – SCHEMAS
docs.text:
Model: SearchRequest

Field Type Required Constraints Description acknowledgmentNumber string No 1–15 alphanumeric, case-insensitive Acknowledgment number filter. applicationID string No 1–15 alphanumeric, case-insensitive Application ID filter. referenceNumber string No 1–15 alphanumeric, case-insensitive Reference number filter. applicationYear integer Yes 2024, 2025, or 2026; default 2026 Application year filter. loanStatus string No Approved, Pending, or Rejected Loan status filter.

SearchRequest

acknowledgmentNumber: string (1–15 alphanumeric) referenceNumber: string (1–15 alphanumeric) applicationId: string (1–15 alphanumeric) loanStatus: string (enum: Approved, Pending, Rejected) applicationYear: number (required, enum: 2024 | 2025 | 2026; default=2026)

Query parameters

Parameter Type Required Constraints Description sortBy string No submissionDate, amount, or customerName Field used to sort results. sortOrder string No asc or desc; default desc Sort direction.

Model: SearchResponse

Field Type Description status string Search result status. applications array Matching loan application records.

SearchResponse

status: `string`
applications: `array<ApplicationRecord>`

Model: ApplicationRecord

Field Type Description applicationId string Unique loan application identifier. customerName string Customer’s full name. loanType string Type of loan. status string Current application status. amount number Loan amount requested or approved. submittedBy string Officer who submitted the application. submissionDate string Submission date in YYYY-MM-DD format. branchCode string Branch identifier.

ApplicationRecord

applicationId: `string`
customerName: `string`
loanType: `string`
status: `string`
amount: `number`
submittedBy: `string`
submissionDate: `string (date)`
branchCode: `string`
